task: Add a saveImage tool: given a selector for an (or canvas) in the sandbox tab, read its full-resolution bytes in the page via CDP (works for blob: URLs), send them through the relay, and have the MCP server write them to an absolute path the caller gives; return only {path, bytes, width, height, mimeType}. No downloads permission. Live-verify by saving a generated image from gemini.google.com.

analysis.objective: Add a saveImage page action (the 23rd PAGE_ACTIONS entry) that reads the full-resolution bytes of an or picked by a selector in the sandbox tab — in the page via CDP, including blob: sources — carries them through the relay, and has the MCP server write them to a caller-given absolute path, returning only {path, bytes, width, height, mimeType}; the vision's next slice: a standalone agent-agnostic Chrome bridge that can pull real artifacts out of a page, not just read it.
analysis.successDefinition: Done means all hold: (1) a phase-0 live probe on gemini.google.com in the real signed-in Chrome via the sandbox tab records in discoveries.md which src scheme a generated image actually has (blob:, data:, or cross-origin https) and which in-page/CDP read route returns its bytes, and the reader is built on that recorded route; (2) saveImage is added across the full parity surface — PAGE_ACTIONS 22->23, types, param validation, extension handler, TOOL_CATALOG entry with an additionalProperties:false schema {selector, path, overwrite?}, MCP server branch, README, and the hard-coded action-list/length tests — with tsc, eslint (--max-warnings 0) and vitest green via npm run verify; (3) the MCP server, not the extension, writes the file: a non-absolute path is rejected, and an existing file without overwrite:true returns a clear refusal and is left byte- and mtime-untouched; (4) a successful call's MCP result contains only {path, bytes, width, height, mimeType} — no base64, no image content block — where bytes equals the on-disk file size, width/height are the image's natural (or canvas) pixel dimensions not CSS size, and mimeType matches the written bytes' magic number; (5) defined, non-throwing, distinct outcomes, each unit-tested, for: decoded bytes > 25 MB ('too large', nothing written, measured size + limit reported), selector matches nothing, element is not img/canvas, image not loaded / zero-size, tainted/unreadable source, relative path, existing file without overwrite; (6) manifest.json gains no 'downloads' permission (and no new permission at all) and chrome.downloads is never referenced; (7) live: in a fresh MCP session, saveImage on a Gemini-generated image in the sandbox tab writes a file to an absolute path whose byte count, decoded dimensions and magic-number type match the returned fields and whose dimensions match the in-page naturalWidth/naturalHeight, a second call to the same path without overwrite is refused, and the results are recorded in a dated section of docs/VERIFICATION.md, linked from README — the horizon's last phase stays blocked MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING until this passes.

The read runs in the sandbox tab via CDP Runtime.evaluate (returnByValue + awaitPromise, inside the existing per-command withDebuggerSession, under the 15s CDP cap) — the route the h9 decision lifted the Runtime.evaluate ban for; an in-page fetch(src) of a blob: URL or a draw-to-canvas + toBlob works in the page's own origin; the phase-0 probe confirms which route Gemini needs.

Bytes travel base64-encoded inside the existing command-response frame; the 25 MB decoded cap is ~33.4 MB of base64, well under ws's default 100 MiB maxPayload (relay.ts constructs WebSocketServer with no maxPayload override), so no new relay frame kind is needed.
The 25 MB check runs in-page/extension-side before the base64 payload crosses the relay, so an oversized payload is never moved (matching the h12 in-page bounding decision).
The MCP server process can write to any absolute path the OS user can write; a missing parent directory is a defined error, not silently created.

For a canvas, the saved bytes are the canvas re-encoded as PNG (toBlob) and 'full resolution' means its backing-store width/height; for an img, the bytes are the original resource bytes, not re-encoded.
The 30s controller DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS and the 15s CDP cap suffice for a single generated image of <= 25 MB on localhost.

Writing to a caller-supplied path is a file-write primitive: without the absolute-path check, overwrite-off-by-default, and a race-safe existence check (exclusive-create open flag rather than check-then-write), a caller could clobber arbitrary files — this invariant must not be traded for convenience.

phases.name: Probe Gemini image source and byte-read route
phases.goal: Find out, on a real Gemini-generated image open in the sandbox tab, which src scheme the image uses (blob:, data: or cross-origin https), which in-page read route returns its full-resolution bytes, and whether the image is loaded and decoded in the unfocused sandbox tab. Write the answer down as a probe report whose verdict either confirms the in-page fetch route that the reader phase plans to use or names the route it must use instead.
phases.rationale: saveImage reads the image bytes inside the page through CDP Runtime.evaluate (CDP is the Chrome DevTools Protocol, which the extension already drives via chrome.debugger). That only works if an in-page fetch(src) or canvas toBlob can reach the bytes. A cross-origin https image hits CORS, and a canvas drawn from it becomes 'tainted', meaning the browser refuses to export its pixels. In that case the reader needs a different CDP route (Page.getResourceContent or Network.getResponseBody), so this has to be known before the reader is built. Horizons 13 and 15 opened with the same kind of probe.
changes: In the user's signed-in Chrome, with a fresh MCP session through Claude Code, put the sandbox tab on a gemini.google.com conversation that shows a generated image, and find a stable CSS selector for that image with the existing snapshot/query tools.

rubric.label: Exactly one machine-checkable verdict
rubric.ruleStatement: The probe report ends in exactly one verdict line that a script can parse, and a REPLAN verdict names a concrete CDP route. 10 = one verdict line, last line of the file, and a REPLAN names the exact CDP method plus the measured reason; 8 = one valid verdict line; minScore 7 allows a valid verdict with a terse reason.
passCriteria: Run `grep -cE '^VERDICT: (PROCEED in-page-fetch|REPLAN .+)$' docs/probes/save-image-gemini-probe.md`. It prints exactly 1.

phases.name: Add CDP image reader to debugger ports
phases.goal: Give the extension's DebuggerPorts a readImage(tabId, selector) method. Inside one per-command debugger session it reads the selected element with a Runtime.evaluate (kind, complete, currentSrc, naturalWidth/naturalHeight, or canvas width/height). For an , it returns the exact resource bytes the page loaded via CDP Page.getResourceContent(main frameId, currentSrc), and the 25 MB cap is checked in the extension before the result leaves readImage. For a , it returns toBlob('image/png') bytes with the cap checked in the page. The result is a typed ImageReadResult whose failure reasons are distinct.
phases.rationale: The live probe showed in-page fetch(currentSrc) fails on Gemini (the lh3 https copy is CORS-blocked and the blob: copy is revoked) and the https canvas is tainted. Page.getResourceContent reads the resource the frame already loaded, so it does not depend on page CORS, and it returns the file the page loaded without re-encoding, which the user chose as the contract. The evaluate/coerce path caps at 1,000,000 characters and double-serialises, so readImage needs its own narrow CDP chain and guards. Checking the cap inside readImage means oversized bytes never reach the relay. getResourceContent cannot be run live until saveImage is registered and the MCP writer exists, so the live-verify phase does that check, and 'unreadable' makes a failure there visible instead of a crash.
changes: In src/protocol/types.ts, add the ImageReadResult discriminated union, modelled on CaptureTabFailureResult. Success is { read: true, base64, mimeType?, width, height, byteLength }: mimeType is 'image/png' for canvas and absent for img, because getResourceContent reports none and the MCP side sniffs it. Failure is { read: false, reason: 'element-not-found' | 'not-image' | 'not-loaded' | 'tainted' | 'unreadable' | 'too-large', size?, limit? }. Do not add any Record<PageAction,…> key yet.

In debugger-ports.ts, add readImage(tabId, selector): Promise<ImageReadResult> to the DebuggerPorts interface and its chrome.debugger implementation. Run every CDP call in one withDebuggerSession run closure under the 15 s CDP cap, and add 'reading image' to the session label union.

Step 1, element probe: send a Runtime.evaluate (returnByValue, awaitPromise) whose expression is built with JSON.stringify(selector), never by concatenation, in the try/catch style of buildElementRectExpression. It returns {found, kind:'img'|'canvas'|'other', complete, currentSrc, naturalWidth, naturalHeight} for img, or the canvas width/height. Narrow the reply with an isRecord-based hand-written guard. Map no element to 'element-not-found', other tags to 'not-image', and an img that is not complete or has zero natural size (or a zero-size canvas) to 'not-loaded'.

Step 2, img: send Page.enable defensively, then Page.getFrameTree, and narrow frameTree.frame.id (main frame) with a hand-written guard that throws a clear Error if it is missing. Then send Page.getResourceContent({frameId, url: currentSrc}) and narrow it to {content: string, base64Encoded: boolean}. Map a CDP error from getResourceContent, empty content, or base64Encoded:false (a text resource) to { read:false, reason:'unreadable' }. Do not use an in-page fetch and do not fall back to canvas for img. width/height are naturalWidth/naturalHeight.

Add a module-private MAX_SAVE_IMAGE_BYTES = 25 * 1024 * 1024. For img, compute the decoded byte length from the base64 (length*3/4 minus padding) right after getResourceContent, in debugger-ports.ts. When it exceeds the cap, return { read:false, reason:'too-large', size, limit } with no base64.

Step 2, canvas: run a separate Runtime.evaluate that calls toBlob('image/png'). It compares blob.size with the cap in the page before FileReader base64 encoding and returns only {tooLarge, size} when over. A toBlob SecurityError maps to 'tainted'. Narrow the reply with its own guard; do not route it through evaluate()/cdpEvalOutcome.
Add a readImage stub to both full DebuggerPorts fakes (page-actions.unit.test.ts fakeDebugger and fakeDebuggerPorts in service-worker.unit.test.ts).

In debugger-ports.unit.test.ts, use a method-dispatching sendCommand stub (Page.enable / Page.getFrameTree / Runtime.evaluate / Page.getResourceContent) to test: img success (base64 passed through, natural size, no mimeType), canvas success, element-not-found, not-image, not-loaded, tainted (canvas), unreadable for a getResourceContent error, for empty content and for base64Encoded:false, too-large for img (extension-side, at the limit and limit+1) and for canvas, getResourceContent called with the main frame id and url === currentSrc, a malformed getFrameTree or evaluate reply throwing, and a timeout. Assert that detach runs on every path and that the selector reaches the expression only JSON-encoded.

rubric.label: Each failure reason is reachable on its own and is the right one
rubric.ruleStatement: Each of the six ImageReadResult failure reasons ('element-not-found', 'not-image', 'not-loaded', 'tainted', 'unreadable', 'too-large') comes from exactly one condition and has its own test, and environment faults (a malformed reply, a timeout, a missing frame id) throw instead of being reported as one of these outcomes. 10 = every reason and every 'unreadable' cause has its own test that asserts the exact reason value, and no two conditions share one branch by accident. 8 = all six reasons are tested with exact values, with at most one small gap, such as a zero-size canvas not tested on its own. Below 7 = a reason has no test, or two different conditions give the same reason when the contract keeps them apart.
passCriteria: Run `npx vitest run src/extension/debugger-ports.unit.test.ts`: it passes, and the readImage tests include one case per reason (element-not-found, not-image, not-loaded, tainted, unreadable, too-large), each asserting `reason` with toEqual/toBe on the exact string.

'unreadable' has three separate tests: (a) Page.getResourceContent rejects with a CDP error, (b) it returns content '' , and (c) it returns base64Encoded:false. Each one resolves to { read:false, reason:'unreadable' } and does not reject.

'not-loaded' is tested for an with complete:false or naturalWidth 0. 'tainted' is tested only for a whose toBlob throws a SecurityError. An never produces 'tainted' (check the img branch in src/extension/debugger-ports.ts).

A malformed Runtime.evaluate reply, a getFrameTree reply with no frameTree.frame.id, and a timeout each make readImage REJECT with an Error. None of them resolves to { read:false, ... }, and the tests assert the rejection with `rejects.toThrow`.
The ImageReadResult failure `reason` in src/protocol/types.ts is a closed string-literal union of exactly these six values, not `string`.
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: the getResourceContent call is wrapped in a broad try/catch, so a malformed getFrameTree reply is also reported as 'unreadable' and a protocol bug looks like a page-content problem.
An with complete:false falls through to getResourceContent and comes back as 'unreadable' rather than 'not-loaded'.
base64Encoded:false is not checked, so a text/SVG resource's raw text is returned as if it were base64.
The test for a missing element only asserts `read === false` and never checks the reason.

rubric.label: The 25 MB cap is enforced inside readImage, and the boundary is exact
rubric.ruleStatement: Oversized bytes never leave readImage. For an , the extension computes the decoded byte length from the base64, correcting for padding, right after getResourceContent and compares it with MAX_SAVE_IMAGE_BYTES (25*1024*1024). For a , the page compares blob.size with the cap before FileReader encodes it. A too-large result carries size and limit and no base64. 10 = boundary tests at exactly the limit (succeeds) and limit+1 (too-large) for img, a canvas too-large test, and a padding-aware length calculation that a test checks with base64 ending in '=' or '=='. 8 = the cap is in the right places and both boundary tests exist. Below 7 = the cap is missing for one kind, is checked after the result is built, or is off by one.
passCriteria: `grep -n "MAX_SAVE_IMAGE_BYTES" src/extension/debugger-ports.ts` shows one module-private constant equal to 25 * 1024 * 1024 that is not exported, and the img branch uses it before the success object is built.

The img byte length is computed from the base64 string as length*3/4 minus the padding count. A test feeds base64 whose decoded size is exactly 26214400 and gets read:true, and a test with 26214401 gets { read:false, reason:'too-large', size:26214401, limit:26214400 }.
No too-large result has a `base64` property. The tests assert this with `not.toHaveProperty('base64')` or an exact toEqual.

The canvas toBlob expression in src/extension/debugger-ports.ts compares blob.size with the limit before FileReader/readAsDataURL runs, and returns only {tooLarge, size} when over. A canvas too-large test maps that reply to reason 'too-large' with size and limit.
The cap value is inlined into the canvas expression as a number. No in-page variable controls it.
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: the img byte length is taken as base64.length*3/4 without removing padding, so an image exactly at the limit with '=' padding is reported as too-large.
The canvas expression encodes the blob to base64 first and checks the size afterwards, so a 200 MB canvas is serialised into the CDP reply.
The too-large result still includes the base64 string, so the bytes reach the relay anyway.
Only a limit+1 test exists, so an off-by-one (>= instead of >) goes unnoticed.

rubric.label: An is read only through Page.getResourceContent on the main frame at currentSrc
rubric.ruleStatement: An is read from the resource the frame already loaded: Page.enable, then Page.getFrameTree (main frame id), then Page.getResourceContent({frameId, url: currentSrc}). The base64 is passed through unchanged with naturalWidth/naturalHeight and no mimeType. There is no in-page fetch and no canvas fallback. 10 = a test asserts the exact getResourceContent params and that the returned base64 is byte-identical, and a test proves no Runtime.evaluate call contains fetch(. 8 = the route and params are asserted. Below 7 = the img path re-encodes, fetches, or falls back to canvas, or uses the wrong frame or url.
passCriteria: `grep -nE "fetch\(|drawImage|toDataURL" src/extension/debugger-ports.ts` finds no match inside the readImage img path.
A test asserts that sendCommand was called with 'Page.getResourceContent' and params exactly { frameId: <frameTree.frame.id from the stub>, url: <currentSrc from the probe stub> }.
A test asserts that Page.enable and Page.getFrameTree are sent before Page.getResourceContent, in that order, using the order of the sendCommand spy's calls.

The img success test asserts toEqual { read:true, base64:<stub content unchanged>, width:naturalWidth, height:naturalHeight, byteLength } and that `mimeType` is absent. The canvas success test asserts mimeType 'image/png' and the canvas width/height.

The frameId is taken from the first child frame, or the url is the img's `src` attribute instead of `currentSrc`, so a srcset image reads the wrong resource.
The img result sets mimeType:'image/png' as a default, so the MCP side never sniffs the real type.

rubric.label: One debugger session, detached on every outcome
rubric.ruleStatement: Each readImage call runs all of its CDP commands inside one withDebuggerSession run labelled 'reading image', under the 15 s cap, and the debugger is detached after every outcome: success, each failure reason, a malformed reply, a CDP rejection, and a timeout. 10 = every readImage test asserts detachSpy was called with the tabId, a test asserts attach was called exactly once per readImage call, and the timeout test uses fake timers and asserts both the rejection message and the detach. 8 = detach is asserted on the success, failure, malformed and timeout paths. Below 7 = any path is untested for detach, or readImage attaches more than once.
passCriteria: In src/extension/debugger-ports.unit.test.ts, every readImage `it(...)` block contains `expect(detachSpy).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ tabId: <id> })`. Count the readImage tests and the detach assertions with grep, or by reading the readImage describe block.
A test asserts attachSpy was called exactly once for a full img read (Page.enable + getFrameTree + getResourceContent + evaluate), which proves one session.
A timeout test (vi.useFakeTimers, with sendCommand never resolving) asserts a rejection whose message contains 'timed out' and 'reading image', and asserts detach.
`grep -n "reading image" src/extension/debugger-ports.ts` shows the label in the withDebuggerSession label union and in the readImage call.
No readImage code path calls chrome.debugger.attach or chrome.debugger.detach directly. All of them go through withDebuggerSession.
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: readImage makes two withDebuggerSession calls, one for the probe evaluate and one for getResourceContent, so the debugger attaches twice and the Chrome banner flickers.
Detach is asserted only in the success test, and the 'unreadable'-from-CDP-rejection path is never checked for detach.
The timeout test uses real timers with a short timeoutMs override and does not assert the label in the error message.

rubric.label: Every CDP reply is narrowed by a guard, and the selector is only ever JSON-encoded
rubric.ruleStatement: The replies from Runtime.evaluate (probe and toBlob), Page.getFrameTree and Page.getResourceContent are typed unknown and narrowed with isRecord-based hand-written guards that reject wrong types. The selector reaches page JavaScript only through JSON.stringify. 10 = a separate malformed-reply test for each of the three reply kinds asserts a rejection with a clear message, and a test with a selector containing quotes, a backslash and `</script>` proves it is inert. 8 = the guards exist, at least two malformed-reply tests exist, and a JSON-encoding test exists. Below 7 = a reply is read with a cast or optional chaining without a type check, or the selector is concatenated into the expression.
passCriteria: `grep -nE "as (\{|Record|Image|string)|!\." src/extension/debugger-ports.ts` finds no cast or non-null assertion in the readImage code or its guards. The guards use isRecord and typeof checks.
A test passes a selector such as `a"]');alert(1);//` and asserts that the Runtime.evaluate expression sent contains `JSON.stringify(selector)` verbatim and no unescaped copy of the selector.

Separate tests feed a malformed probe reply (e.g. result.value missing `found`), a getFrameTree reply without frameTree.frame.id, and a getResourceContent reply where `content` is not a string. Each one rejects with an Error whose message names the CDP method or stage, and each one detaches.
A getResourceContent reply with content of the right type but base64Encoded:false resolves to 'unreadable', not a throw. This shows the guard checks shape and the mapper decides the outcome.

The canvas toBlob reply has its own guard and does not reuse evaluate()/cdpEvalOutcome or the 1,000,000-character coerce path: `grep -n "cdpEvalOutcome" src/extension/debugger-ports.ts` shows no call inside readImage.
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: the getFrameTree reply is narrowed with `isRecord(reply) && isRecord(reply.frameTree)` but frame.id is read without checking that it is a string, so a numeric or undefined id is passed on to getResourceContent.
The probe expression is built with a template literal `document.querySelector('${selector}')`, so a selector containing a quote breaks out.
The canvas path reuses the shared evaluate() helper, so a 2 MB PNG is cut off by the 1 MB coerce cap and reported as a generic error.
A malformed reply makes the code throw a TypeError ('cannot read properties of undefined') instead of a clear guard error.

phases.healerHint: The most likely miss is in the tests, not the code: some readImage paths (the three 'unreadable' causes, the malformed getFrameTree reply, the timeout) don't assert detachSpy, or there is no exact-limit/limit+1 img boundary test with base64 padding. phases.name: Add MCP image writer and saveImage server branch
phases.goal: Make the MCP server, not the extension, write the image to disk. A new image writer (src/mcp/image-writer.ts) does an exclusive-create write and sniffs the MIME type from the file's magic number. A saveImage branch in handleToolCall checks that the path is absolute, strips path and overwrite before forwarding {selector}, narrows the image read result, writes the bytes, and returns only {path, bytes, width, height, mimeType}.
phases.rationale: Writing to a caller-given path is a file-write primitive, so the absolute-path check, overwrite-off-by-default, and a race-safe exclusive create (open flag 'wx' rather than check-then-write) must all live in one tested place. No src file does filesystem I/O today. A small writer injected through McpServerDeps keeps node:fs out of the pure server mapper and lets server tests use a fake. The writer and the branch are one small slice of one subsystem (the MCP server) across layers, and nothing else consumes the writer.
changes: Create src/mcp/image-writer.ts with writeImageFile(path, bytes, overwrite) using node:fs/promises open with flag 'wx' (or 'w' only when overwrite is true). It returns { written: true, bytes } or a refusal { written: false, reason: 'exists' | 'parent-missing' | 'io-error', message } and never creates directories. Also add sniffMimeType(bytes) for PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF magic numbers.

In image-writer.unit.test.ts, use fs.mkdtemp to test: a fresh write; an existing file without overwrite is refused with its bytes and mtime unchanged; overwrite:true replaces the file; a missing parent directory gives 'parent-missing'; each sniffed format; unknown bytes.

Decode base64 with Buffer.from, let the sniffed MIME type win over the page-reported type, write through the writer, map a refusal to isError, and on success return text JSON with exactly {path, bytes, width, height, mimeType}, with no image block and no base64.

rubric.label: Success result is exactly {path, bytes, width, height, mimeType}
